title: Risk first, returns second: start every trade with the max loss
summary: When markets rise, people talk about gains; when they fall, they go quiet or panic. The speaker starts each decision from the maximum downside: how much can I lose, before how much can I gain. That builds a solid base for decisions, and good decisions compound alongside returns.

steps.caption: The gain you need to recover from a loss.
The curve rises faster than the loss: deep losses need very large gains to recover.
A 30% loss needs about a 43% gain just to get back to even.
Drag the loss slider: a 50% loss needs a 100% gain.
That is why the speaker asks first: what is my maximum downside?

takeaways: Ask how much you can lose before you ask how much you can gain.
Knowing the max downside makes decisions calmer when markets fall.
Good decision making compounds alongside returns.
caveats: The recovery chart is added to illustrate the idea; the clip gives no numbers.
The clip ends with a follow and link-in-bio request.
